attempts.summary: Created a sandboxed systemd service `inventory-worker` on node1 running a long-lived worker loop as a dedicated unprivileged user, confined via ProtectSystem=strict + ReadWritePaths=/var/lib/inventory and NoNewPrivileges=yes (plus additional hardening: PrivateTmp, PrivateDevices, ProtectKernelTunables/Modules, RestrictSUIDSGID, LockPersonality, MemoryDenyWriteExecute, empty CapabilityBoundingSet/AmbientCapabilities). Verified the service writes only inside /var/lib/inventory and that NoNewPrivs=1 is enforced on the live process. Falsified the sandbox by running an equivalent transient unit that successfully wrote inside /var/lib/inventory but failed with 'Read-only file system' writing to /etc. Completed the mandatory node1 restart protocol: captured healthy baseline (boot_id, uptime, active service, ticking log), issued `systemctl reboot` via a backgrounded acknowledger so the ack returned before disconnection, polled through a connection-timeout window, confirmed boot_id changed (28ae5f98… → 2f82af98…) and uptime start advanced, then verified inventory-worker is enabled+active with a new PID and fresh log tick post-boot, with /var/lib/inventory ownership/permissions intact.
